correctness.rationale: Each dimer intersecting a window contributes one independent fair bit, whether the window sees one or both sites. For length 2m the two phases meet m and m+1 dimers; for 2m+1 they both meet m+1. Their compatibility sets intersect exactly at the two alternating words because the two phases together constrain every adjacent edge. This yields the support counts, the even/odd ambiguity masses, and posteriors 2/3 and 1/2 on overlap; summing the smaller joint mass of each overlap word gives the optimal Bayes risk, including n=1. N exceeds n precisely when the prefix still alternates, and the two geometric sums with the n=0,1 terms give 9/2 symbols. The chain rule subtracts the phase posterior entropy from H(B_n|Phi)+1, yielding the two block entropy formulas and entropy rate 1/2. The adjacent-block information 2H_n−H_(2n) tends to 3/2 and increases to the information of the two full half-lines, which are generated by the increasing finite blocks. Independently, both half-lines determine the phase outside a null set, giving one common bit; conditional on phase, their only possible shared orientation bit is the dimer crossing the cut, present with probability 1/2. This gives the same limit. Separate enumeration agreed for n=1,…,12 (606 positive marginal words; probability comparisons exact, entropy numerical). In the frozen verifier, the label 'positive exact phase-conditioned cylinders' for 606 means positive marginal words, not phase-word pairs. No finite computation proves the infinite formula, and no noisy or biased extension follows.
